title: Visitor

act2.summary: a fourth report (cheap, aligned with the pattern) and then a new record kind (expensive, the pattern's known price)

solutions.title: Reports become visitor classes; records only know how to accept one
solutions.tradeoff: A new report is one new file and zero edits to any record class. The price is symmetric and exact: a new record kind means every existing report class gains a method, and the interface every report implements changes too.

reviewFocus: Does the fourth report (operatorNote) touch any existing record class, or only add one new visitor?
Does the new record kind (DomeRecord) touch every existing report visitor, or does something dodge the interface change?
Is the walkthrough honest that this act 2 is not a win for the pattern overall - it is a win on one half and a real cost on the other?
Does the walkthrough name what would have absorbed the new-record-kind half at zero cost (the very shape act 1 replaced)?
Is `LogRecordVisitor<R>` generic enough that a report returning something other than string/number/boolean (e.g. an array) doesn't need its own bespoke interface?
